title: The root account must be the only account with unrestricted access to TOSS 5 system.
check_content:
Verify only the "root" account has a UID "0" assignment using the following command:

$ awk -F: '$3 == 0 {print $1}' /etc/passwd

root

If any accounts other than "root" have a UID of "0", this is a finding.
fixtext:
Change the UID of any account on the system, other than root, that has a UID of "0". 

If the account is associated with system commands or applications, the UID should be changed to one greater than "0" but less than "1000". Otherwise, assign a UID of greater than "1000" that has not already been assigned.
VulnDiscussion: An account has root authority if it has a user identifier (UID) of "0". Multiple accounts with a UID of "0" afford more opportunity for potential intruders to guess a password for a privileged account. Properly configuring sudo is recommended to afford multiple system administrators (SAs) access to root privileges in an accountable manner.
